name: Erromintxela
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Mixed Basque-Romani; Wikipedia phonology section is segmental only, no stress statement; no grammar found

sources.citation: Baudrimont, A. (1862). Vocabulaire de la langue des Bohémiens habitant les pays basques français. Bordeaux: Académie Impériale des Sciences. (Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive description 'phonology or text collection', 27 pp.)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Intro pp. 10-13 gives informants, an 'alphabet bohémien' (8 vowels, 20 consonants) with segmental comparisons to French/Spanish/Greek/Basque, and the Basque article -a; nothing at all on accent or stress (a full-text search for stress/accent/tonique/syllabe: no hit).

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive descriptions: Ackerley 1929 (grammar sketch, 45 pp) and Baudrimont 1862 (phonology or text collection, 27 pp); the Harvard library catalogue: Ackerley online via ProQuest only; Bakker 1991 not found anywhere.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Consonant/vowel tables only (from Baudrimont/Azkue/Lhande materials); no stress or prosody statement; bibliography lists Baudrimont 1862, Berraondo 1921, Krutwig 1986, Vizarraga 2001, Argia 2003/2008 pieces, Muñoz & Lopez de Mungia via Argia.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: §Fonologia: 'Egun, ez dago hizkuntzaren deskribapen fonologikoa erakusten duen paradigmarik' (today there is no phonological description of the language); no stress statement.

sources.citation: Krinková, Zuzana (2013). Vzájemné ovlivňování romštiny, španělštiny a dalších jazyků Pyrenejského poloostrova [The mutual influence of Romani, Spanish and the other languages of the Iberian Peninsula]. PhD dissertation, Charles University, Prague, 318 pp. + appendices (Czech). http://hdl.handle.net/20.500.11956/59425
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p. 69 (ch. 3.2 transcription conventions): stress marking follows each source; 'problematiku přízvuku v iberských pararomštinách ponecháváme na případnou budoucí studii' (we leave the problem of stress in Iberian Para-Romani varieties to a possible future study); general remark only that the probable Early Romani stress is fairly well attested in Iberian (Para-)Romani (e.g. Caló adjectives ending in a stressed vowel). Erromintxela/errumantxela mentioned only 6 times (two Bakker 1991 example sentences on p. ~40); no Erromintxela stress statement.

sources.citation: Agirrezabal, Lore (2003-09-28). Erromintxela, euskal ijitoen hizkera. Argia 1913.
sources.note: Journalistic piece on Josune Muñoz's Kale Dor Kayiko study; says only that the language 'oso bizkor hitz egiten da' (is spoken very fast) and that morphology/verbs are Basque with local dialect features; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Vizarraga, Óscar (2001). Erromintxela: notas para una investigación sociolingüística. O Tchatchipen 33: 35-39.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sociolinguistic report (two generations of speakers, Basque-like social structure); lists 'transcripción fonética de todas las voces recopiladas' as pending work; nothing on stress or phonology.

sources.citation: Bakker, Peter (1991). Basque Romani - a preliminary grammatical sketch of a mixed language. In P. Bakker & M. Cortiade (eds), In the margin of Romani: Gypsy languages in contact, 56-90. Amsterdam: Publikaties van het Instituut voor Algemene Taalwetenschap 58.

sources.note: The only modern grammatical sketch by a linguist with own fieldwork/informant data (Krinková's wordlists cite a 'BASK (Bakker)' column); the most likely place for a phonology section including stress.
